easy.explanation: Job says, “My lips shall not speak wickedness, nor my tongue utter deceit.”
easy.q: What does Job promise that he will not speak?

easy.explanation: Job says, “Till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.”
easy.q: Until when does Job say he will not remove his integrity?

easy.explanation: Job says, “My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go.”
easy.q: What does Job say that he holds fast?

answers: He will not confess to sins he did not commit
He does not want to speak with them
medium.explanation: Job says, “God forbid that I should justify you,” and declares that he will not give up his integrity.
medium.q: Why does Job refuse to justify his friends?

medium.explanation: In this context, Job’s integrity refers to his upright and blameless way of life.
medium.q: What does the word “integrity” mean in “I will not remove mine integrity from me”?

answers: Both express his determination to remain faithful to his integrity
Both show that he has abandoned his faith
medium.explanation: Job swears that he will not speak deceit and declares that he will hold firmly to his righteousness until death.
medium.q: How does Job’s oath relate to his statement about righteousness?

answers: Job believes his heart has not accused him throughout his life
Job asks his friends to forgive him
Job admits that his whole life has been filled with sin
challenge.explanation: Job presents his heart as not condemning him for the way he has lived.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the words “my heart shall not reproach me, so long as I live”?

answers: Job’s integrity versus the accusations against him
challenge.explanation: Job rejects the expectation that he should admit guilt and emphasizes his integrity.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in Job’s words in these verses?

answers: His desire to hide his words
challenge.explanation: Swearing by the living God reinforces the seriousness and firmness of Job’s words.
challenge.q: What does the oath “As God liveth” emphasize at the beginning of Job’s speech?

answers: His enemy and the one who rises against him
easy.explanation: Job says, “Let mine enemy be as the wicked, and he that riseth up against me as the unrighteous.”
easy.q: Whom does Job wish would be treated as the wicked?

easy.explanation: Job asks, “For what is the hope of the hypocrite?” showing that the wicked have no lasting hope.
easy.q: What does the wicked person lack, according to Job?

answers: The reality about which he was speaking
easy.explanation: Job tells them, “Behold, all ye yourselves have seen it.”

answers: God does not hear his cry, and he does not delight himself in the Almighty
medium.explanation: Job asks whether God will hear the wicked person’s cry and whether he will delight himself in the Almighty.
medium.q: Why does Job say that the wicked person has no true hope?

medium.explanation: In this context, a hypocrite is a wicked or insincere person whose hope is ultimately empty.
medium.q: What does “hypocrite” mean in the phrase “the hope of the hypocrite”?

answers: They have seen the reality, so they have no reason to speak empty words
They did not hear him, so he must be silent
They are too wealthy to understand money
medium.explanation: Job says that his friends have seen these things themselves, yet they still speak vainly.
medium.q: How do Job’s words in verse 12 lead to criticism of his friends?

answers: He applies the fate described for the wicked to his enemies and opponents
He announces that he intends to leave his friends
He shows that his enemies are wealthier than he is
challenge.explanation: Job directs the description of the wicked person’s fate toward his enemies and those who rise against him.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of Job applying the fate of the wicked to his enemies?

answers: He cannot rely on closeness to God or on his prayers being heard
He is always surrounded by friends
challenge.explanation: Job asks whether God will hear the wicked person’s cry and whether he will delight himself in the Almighty.
challenge.q: Which claim about the wicked is repeated in different forms in these verses?

answers: You are speaking empty and groundless words
You are speaking in a difficult language
You are speaking about great wealth
challenge.explanation: Job criticizes his friends for speaking vainly even though they have seen the reality for themselves.
challenge.q: What does the expression “ye are all altogether vain” mean in the context of Job’s speech?

paragraphs.title: The Wicked Person’s Portion: Sword, Hunger, and Loss

answers: They will suffer by the sword
easy.explanation: Job says, “If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword.”
easy.q: What will happen to the children of the wicked person, according to Job?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “His offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.”
easy.q: What will the wicked person’s offspring not be satisfied with?

easy.explanation: Job says, “The just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.”
easy.q: To whom will the silver prepared by the wicked person be divided?

answers: Their number does not save them; they may suffer by the sword and hunger
Their number causes them to build a house
medium.explanation: Job describes the children as facing the sword and the offspring as lacking bread.
medium.q: What is the connection between having many children and their fate?

answers: Those who are left of his family or people
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to those who remain of the wicked person’s household or descendants.
medium.q: What does “those that remain of him” mean in “Those that remain of him shall be buried in death”?

answers: The wicked person loses both his family and control of his possessions
The wicked person becomes even richer
The wicked person succeeds in protecting his children
medium.explanation: The passage describes both suffering among his descendants and the loss of his possessions to others.
medium.q: What does the movement from sword and hunger to the division of silver teach?

answers: What the wicked person has gathered or established does not remain under his control
They all belong to his friends
challenge.explanation: His family suffers, and his possessions pass to others rather than remaining under his control.
challenge.q: What common idea applies to the clothing, silver, and descendants in this description?

challenge.explanation: Comparing silver with dust emphasizes its abundance.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “silver as the dust” emphasize?

answers: His possessions eventually pass to others and cannot protect his family
He does not know how to count money
challenge.explanation: Although he heaps up silver and prepares clothing, they do not remain his, and his family suffers.
challenge.q: Why does great wealth not benefit the wicked person in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Rich Man’s Fragile House and End

easy.explanation: His house is compared to a moth and to a booth made by a keeper.
easy.q: What is the wicked person’s house compared to?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered.”
easy.q: What happens to the rich man according to these verses?

answers: Terror, a tempest, and the east wind
easy.explanation: The verses describe terrors, a tempest, and the east wind carrying him away.
easy.q: What carries or drives away the wicked person?

answers: The house is temporary and fragile
The house is large and protected
The house is filled with people
medium.explanation: A moth and a booth suggest something fragile and temporary rather than stable or lasting.
medium.q: What does the comparison of the wicked person’s house to a moth and a booth teach?

medium.explanation: Terrors are frightening experiences or fears that seize the wicked person.
medium.q: What does “terrors” mean in “Terrors take hold on him as waters”?

answers: It emphasizes that he has no stability and is carried away from his place
It shows that he is protected in his house
medium.explanation: The tempest and east wind carry him away and illustrate the loss of his security.
medium.q: How does the storm strengthen the description of the rich man’s end?

answers: Both emphasize the temporary nature of his security and wealth
Both prove that he will remain rich
Both describe the success of his family
challenge.explanation: Neither the house nor the possessions gives him lasting existence or protection.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the disappearance of the rich man’s possessions and his fragile house?

answers: He disappears or dies suddenly, and his wealth cannot save him
He awakens and finds his possessions
He opens his eyes in order to pray
challenge.explanation: The wording presents the rich man’s sudden disappearance or death.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from “he openeth his eyes, and he is not”?

answers: Mockery or a response to his punishment and downfall
A request that he return to his house
challenge.explanation: The people’s response portrays the contempt shown toward him after his downfall.
challenge.q: What do the clapping of hands and hissing at the end express?
